title: Flexible rollout choreography: expressive rules for steps, splits, and rollback thresholds
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Design and implement a flexible, declarative 'choreography' layer for model rollouts that lets product and platform engineers express: traffic splits per step, per-segment schedules (ramp, hold, probe), shadow traffic toggles, perturbation windows, and precise auto-rollback assertions (latency, error rate, quality regression).

Background: Current rollout primitives are rigid (fixed step percentages, coarse guardrails). We need a compact DSL and evaluation engine that can represent common enterprise patterns: canary with progressive ramp and short probes, multi-segment A/B experiments, shadowing with sampled persistence, and automatic rollback when metrics cross thresholds. This ticket scopes the first-pass runtime model + config surface and a policy executor that can run inside both hosted and Dedicated control planes.

Non-goals: Full UI for composing policies (handled in a follow-up PM/UI ticket), advanced ML-driven adaptive step sizing (separate research/Optimize project).

Key design constraints: must be serializable as a single YAML/JSON policy; decision latency for routing must be <2ms in the hot path; evaluation must be replayable for audits; configs should allow safe defaults to prevent accidental 100% flips.
acceptance_criteria: A declarative policy JSON/YAML schema is documented and covers: steps with durations, per-step traffic weights, segment selectors (by route, customer, or token hashing), shadow toggles, probe windows, and rollback assertions.

The policy executor library (Go) implements evaluation and exposes two APIs: EvaluateRoute(request, policy) for hot-path routing decisions and EvaluateSignal(metrics, policy) for periodic assertion checks.

End-to-end test harness that simulates traffic and metric time-series proving rollback triggers and safe holds for at least three canonical scenarios: simple canary ramp, A/B split with continued shadowing, and short probe that escalates to rollback.
Integration PR merged: platform/rollout: add policy parser, executor, and migration shim for existing simple rollouts (PR #4821).
Conformance tests and example policies added to confluence page and repo examples (links in comments).

2026-02-25 - Liam O'Connor: Spike complete. Prototype of policy schema implemented in a playground branch. Trade-offs: keeping the policy expressive vs keeping the evaluation fast. Chose a compact AST with precompiled matchers to keep hot-path cost low.

2026-03-01 - Design review (Priya Desai): Reviewed schema. Feedback: add explicit 'safety_cohort' selector to limit exposure for high-risk customers and support for 'max_concurrent_steps' to avoid overlapping rolls.

2026-03-04 - Eng sync: Decided to implement rollback assertions as pluggable evaluators (latency/error/quality) with a simple threshold comparator for v1. Quality evaluators will accept a reference dataset ID. Logged follow-up for quality infra integration (ENG-31855).
2026-03-08 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821 (adds policy parser + executor skeleton). Requesting review from @maria-ops and @chen-mlinfra.

2026-03-10 - Maria Ops: Left review comments on fallback behaviour when policy parsing fails. Agreed to add a safe-fail default: route 100% to baseline model and emit an alert (incident) instead of failing requests.

2026-03-12 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented unit tests for EvaluateRoute and EvaluateSignal, added example policies under examples/rollouts. Manual canary simulation shows correct weight progression and abort on an injected latency spike.
